items.content:
*Je me suis trompé* — literally "I deceived myself." *Le verre s'est
cassé* — "the glass broke itself."

French routes an enormous amount of ordinary experience through the
reflexive, so things happen *to themselves* rather than being done by
you. English insists on an agent. I keep wondering whether that does
anything to a person over a lifetime, or whether it's just grammar and I
am being romantic about it.

summary: Reflexive verbs route ordinary experience so events happen to themselves.
title: On reflexive verbs and where the blame goes
